material_disagreements_preserved.topic: Whether Table 1's 14.10x headline is merely unreconstructible or actually wrong
positions: REV-2 (T-02): arithmetically inconsistent with Eq. 3. The pure-Q4 floor from split Q16 is 9.755 MiB, above the printed 9.661; using the GDN share recovered from Table 2 (21.4%) the frozen policy should land near 11.61 MiB, i.e. ~11.7x rather than 14.10x.

REV-1, REV-4 and REV-5 each state the opposite: every ratio they recomputed 'reproduces exactly' (136.235/9.661 = 14.10x; 1 - 9.661/136.235 = 92.91%), and REV-4/REV-5 additionally matched 9.660873 / 34.683105 / 136.235352 / 14.1018x digit-for-digit against claim_evidence_map.tsv.
REV-3 also records the internal arithmetic as 'unusually clean' and raises only the un-reconciled 136.235-vs-140.34 denominator gap.
material_disagreements_preserved.recommended_resolution: I verified both sides myself and side with REV-2 on the finding, with a narrower claim than REV-2 states. Unconditional and confirmed: 36 bytes per 64-value Q4 group against 128 at BF16 caps compression at 3.5556x, so a Q4/Q4/Q8 policy cannot reach 3.5900x, and 9.661 MiB sits below its own format floor of 9.755 MiB; the 'same-memory mixed' (3.69x) and 'aggressive mixed' (4.60x) rows exceed even the pure-Q4 ceiling, which is only admissible if those policies use sub-4-bit widths that the paper never states. Conditional and NOT established: REV-2's corrected value of 11.6 MiB / 11.7x, which transfers the eight-item cohort's GDN share into the sixty-item component accounting. The three reviewers who 'verified' the numbers checked ratio consistency and archive agreement, which tests only that the pipeline reproduced its own outputs; neither test touches the format floor, and the artifact index therefore produced a false sense of verification. Note the alternative explanation the authors may have: the component accounting may inflate the split-Q16 numerator (e.g. counting whole underlying storages for unpacked lower-cache tensors) rather than under-count the packed entry. That would rescue the arithmetic but converts the finding into an undisclosed denominator asymmetry between the compared arms, which is equally disqualifying for a headline compression ratio. Only a published per-component byte breakdown resolves which it is.

material_disagreements_preserved.topic: Severity of the mis-implemented dense-recompute arm: fatal to the contribution, or a specification gap
positions: REV-2 (T-01, critical): the interior point does not exist. A Section-3-conformant dense arm gives 7.40 tok/s against Q-CoMem's 7.19 with Store 0.00 and the best F1 in the table, so Q-CoMem is Pareto-dominated and the contribution is a dominated design rather than a trade-off.

REV-4 (R44-4-12, minor; R44-4-04, major): the omission of the adverse TTFT comparison is selective reporting and the dense implementation must be stated, but the finding is framed as a reporting and definition defect.

REV-5 (R44-5-09, major, confidence medium): the arm is 'never operationally defined' and the numbers 'imply' per-token recomputation; the concern extends to the catastrophic-regression rule, which is anchored on the same arm.

REV-1 and REV-3 did not flag the dense TPOT at all; REV-1 instead flagged (Q5) that dense and full-prefix behave very differently against split Q16 in Table 1 (paired CI widths 7.28 vs 0.18) with the explanation buried in a Table 18 footnote.
material_disagreements_preserved.recommended_resolution: I confirm REV-2's arithmetic and adopt its severity. Verified: TPOT 648.75 ms equals TTFT 0.649 s to 0.04%; tok/s = n/(TTFT + n x TPOT) with n between 7.50 and 8.02 reproduces all six Table 2 throughputs, so 648.75 ms is a genuine per-decode-step cost and not an aggregate; substituting the stack's normal 54.11 ms decode gives 8/(0.649 + 8 x 0.05411) = 7.39 tok/s against Q-CoMem's 7.18, alongside a lower TTFT (0.649 vs 0.674) and a higher F1 (39.42 vs 39.01). Q-CoMem is therefore dominated on all four measured axes by a correctly implemented zero-storage baseline on this slice. Two qualifications I attach against REV-2. First, the corrected dense figure is an inference from other rows, not a measurement, so it establishes that the arm must be re-run, not that the corrected numbers are these. Second, REV-2's corroboration from Table 19 (SGLang 0.5.17 with prefix reuse off: TTFT 0.283 s, TPOT 53.38 ms, 12.73 tok/s, F1 39.14 on the identical eight items -- which I verified is in the PDF) is cross-runtime and the paper's own non-pooling discipline forbids quantitative use of it; I treat it as qualitative corroboration only. REV-1's Q5 is a separate and also-valid finding about the same arm on the quality panel and should be fixed together with it. I preserve REV-4's and REV-5's lower severity as a legitimate reading of what is *printed*, but the consequence of the printed numbers is decision-changing, so this is critical, not minor.

material_disagreements_preserved.topic: What the ForkAudit scope gap implies for the contribution, and whether appendix disclosure is sufficient
positions: REV-3 (C1, critical): a structural failure of the motivation-method-experiment chain; the Experiments section tests a different artifact from the one the Methodology describes, and the seam is invisible unless the reader collates page 7, page 14 and page 27.

REV-2 (T-03, major): mechanically and not just rhetorically wrong, because the Read path introduces obligations (dequantized-view immutability, residual-chunk binding, packed-entry lifetime) that none of the seven targets in Table 6 can have tested.
REV-1 (Q3, major): the paper's most rigorous evidence does not attach to the system the paper is about, which is why the significance case is narrow.
REV-4 and REV-5, both with repository access, treat the gap primarily as a disclosure and attribution matter and locate the qualification in Appendix H and Table 5's exclusion column.
material_disagreements_preserved.recommended_resolution: Uphold the critical severity, and explicitly preserve the access-mode point. Appendix H's phrase '16-bit KV' on page 27 and Table 5's exclusion column do not make the main text self-contained: the abstract, Figure 1's audit rail and contribution bullet 3 present the audit as validating the Q-CoMem Read path, and a pdf-only reader who stops at the main text will conclude the shipped quantized path has been ownership-audited. That a repository reviewer can confirm the exclusion validates the authors' honesty; it does not repair the PDF. Two distinct remedies exist and they are not equivalent: the writing fix (state the audited precision, runtime and absence of a split depth at every point where ownership safety is claimed, and add the exclusion to Table 5 and Section 5.6) removes the misreading but permanently caps the ownership contribution at 'a validated methodology for hybrid shared-document serving, evaluated on a full-prefix BF16 configuration'; the experiment fix (one ForkAudit cell on the packed Q4/Q4/Q8 Read path with targets for dequantized-view immutability and residual-chunk binding) is what would let contribution bullet 3 stand as written. Authors should choose deliberately and the choice should be visible in the abstract.

material_disagreements_preserved.topic: Whether ForkAudit's flagship historical-alias result demonstrates detection value or only localization value
positions: REV-1, REV-2 and REV-3 (all pdf_only) name it the strongest verified contribution: output equality, FP32 logits, terminal request GDN state and logical KV are all exact in 8/8 cells while the persistent base is corrupted, and token equality catches 0/5 and exact logits 1/5 of the semantic-complete mutants.

REV-4 (R44-4-11) and REV-5 (R44-5-11), both artifact-aware, note that Table 14's 'Base inv.' column fails 3/3 and 5/5 on the pre-fix path, so a conventional persistent-base content invariant catches the defect in all eight cells, and that Appendix H itself says ForkAudit contributes 'localization rather than exclusive detection'. REV-4 adds that the artifact contains a less favourable conventional-suite comparison (21/22 vs 22/22) marked as not used by the manuscript.
material_disagreements_preserved.recommended_resolution: Both readings are correct and neither should be averaged away. I verified Table 14: 'Base inv.' fails 3/3 and 5/5 pre-fix and passes 3/3 and 5/5 repaired, and its caption already calls it 'a conventional state-invariant catch'. Nothing in the abstract is false -- the alias genuinely is invisible to output equality -- but the main text nowhere carries its own appendix's qualification, so a nine-page reader over-reads the audit's marginal value. This is a claim-narrowing fix, not an evidence defect: one clause in Section 5.5 and, if space allows, the abstract, stating that a persistent-base content invariant also detects this defect and that the audit's increment is authenticated transition-time owner/layer/family localization. On REV-4's asymmetry point I go halfway: excluding the internal conventional-suite matrix may be principled, but if it is excluded then the favourable 0/5 and 1/5 conventional-detector comparisons must carry the same 'not a head-to-head detection study' caveat in the main text rather than only in Appendix H.

material_disagreements_preserved.topic: Reproducibility posture: is the missing method provenance for the named contribution critical or minor?
positions: REV-5 (R44-5-01, R44-5-02, both critical): the reproducibility apparatus resolves to a package never made available, and none of the 83 method_provenance rows covers the quantizer, the Write/Read paths, the policy definitions, the Store accountant, the F1 scorer or the bootstrap.
REV-4 (R44-4-15, minor): frames the same file's staleness and 'pending' statuses as a traceability blemish that does not make any reported number wrong.
REV-1, REV-2 and REV-3 could not see the repository and instead flagged the archival 60-item run's admitted lack of a pre-run source ledger and model-weight ledger.
material_disagreements_preserved.recommended_resolution: Side with REV-5 on severity while adopting REV-4's framing of consequence. I verified the file: 83 rows, zero occurrences of 'quantiz', 'dequant', 'residual', 'bootstrap' or 'LongBench'; the sole deployment row (M-H20-DEPLOYMENT-DERIVATION) points at scripts/generate_h20_deployment_table.py, a formatter over an already-frozen summary; the three C-QCOMEM-60-* claims carry no manuscript location; and Table 2's TTFT/TPOT/most cell values appear nowhere in the claim index. I also confirmed the PDF contains no artifact-availability statement of any kind (no 'supplementary', 'available at', 'github', 'zenodo', or URL). This does not make any number wrong and there is no suggestion of misconduct -- the archival gap is disclosed repeatedly and correctly -- but it inverts the paper's own thesis: a submission arguing that implementations diverge silently from their described semantics leaves the described semantics of its own named method unbacked by any code reference. The pdf-only reviewers' independent discomfort about the archival run is the same finding seen from the other side and should not be discounted because artifact reviewers could see more.

unsupported_reviewer_claims.reviewer_issue_id: R44-REV-2 T-02 (the specific corrected headline '11.73x' / 11.61 MiB)
unsupported_reviewer_claims.reason: The unconditional part survives and I confirm it: 9.661 MiB is below the 9.755 MiB pure-Q4 format floor implied by Eq. 3 and Figure 2c. The specific corrected value does not: it imports the GDN share (21.4%) recovered from Table 2's byte-range-union accounting into Table 1's component accounting, and Section 5.1 states those implementations differ. The authors must publish the component breakdown; they must not be required to print 11.73x.

unsupported_reviewer_claims.reviewer_issue_id: R44-REV-1 Q1 / R44-REV-4 R44-4-02 (the specific claim that the honest advantage falls to 'roughly 3.9x' / 'approximately 3.5x')
unsupported_reviewer_claims.reason: The byte arithmetic is correct and I reproduce it: at 4.5 effective bits per value, full-prefix Q4 is 136.235 x 36/128 = 38.3 MiB, giving 3.97x over the printed 9.661 (and 3.30x over a floor-respecting ~11.6 MiB); a Q4/Q4/Q8-style full-prefix entry is ~45.6 MiB, giving 4.72x. But the projection holds only on the capacity axis: it assumes a quantized full-prefix arm suffers no additional quality loss from packing all ten attention layers' KV, which is exactly what is unmeasured. Asserted from a reviewer-side search under pdf_only access and not verifiable from anything in the review record; REV-1 itself concedes none is prior art at this submission date. unsupported_reviewer_claims.reason: Third-person citation of the prior work one builds on is standard ICLR practice and is not an anonymity defect; treating it as one would penalise correct credit assignment, which is one of this paper's genuine strengths. unsupported_reviewer_claims.reason: I recomputed the implied generated-token counts for Table 19 under tok/s = n/(TTFT + n x TPOT): vLLM off ~9.2, SGLang off ~11.2, HYPIC prefix cache ~31.5. The constructive half of the issue is accepted: state how many of the 24 computed intervals are displayed and why, and add a per-item regression rate at a substantively informative threshold alongside -- not instead of -- the registered rule.

unsupported_reviewer_claims.reviewer_issue_id: R44-REV-5 R44-5-01 (characterisation that ~40% of the results section is 'testimony')
unsupported_reviewer_claims.reason: The underlying finding is confirmed and material -- I verified the PDF contains no availability statement of any kind, and the two supplied index files cannot corroborate the Section 5.5 counts -- but the rhetorical scaling is not supported: the paper does bind its counts to internal hashes and manifests, and the counts are arithmetically self-consistent everywhere three reviewers checked. The actionable requirement is an artifact-availability paragraph and a resolvable index, not a wholesale discount of Section 5.5.

score_gaming_suggestions_to_reject: Deleting or footnoting away the 'no-cache dense recompute' row rather than re-running it. The adverse comparison is the finding; removing the arm removes the paper's own motivating endpoint and would make Section 3 unsupported.

Restating 14.10x under a renamed denominator, or moving it from the abstract to Section 5.2, without publishing the component byte breakdown that shows how a Q4/Q4/Q8 policy achieves 3.59x under a 3.5556x format ceiling.

Responding to the ForkAudit scope gap by removing Figure 1's audit rail or softening the figure caption while leaving the abstract's ForkAudit sentence and contribution bullet 3 unchanged. The scope statement must appear where the claim is made.

Dropping the 'aggressive mixed' and 'same-memory mixed' rows to avoid publishing their bit vectors, rather than specifying them. Those rows currently carry the Section 5.4 argument for the headline policy.

Adding a quantized full-prefix row computed analytically and then comparing its analytic bytes against the measured Q-CoMem Store, or reporting it without F1. The two arms must share a denominator and a quality measurement or the comparison is not a comparison.

Replacing the pooled -0.39 with a per-dataset number chosen after seeing both, or re-selecting the headline policy after per-dataset results arrive. Selection on the reporting data is already an open issue (T-11); compounding it would be worse than leaving the pooled figure.

Adding an artifact-availability sentence that promises release without shipping the quantizer, Write/Read paths and Store accountant, since those are exactly the components method_provenance.tsv currently omits.
Answering the missing capacity experiment (A13) by adding a paragraph asserting that a 14x Store reduction implies ~14x more resident documents. Section 5.6 already, correctly, denies that inference.
must_resolve_before_accept: A1 -- Table 1's Store values must be reconciled with the format floor implied by Eq. 3 and Figure 2c, with a published per-component byte breakdown. A headline compression factor that cannot be derived from the paper's own method section, and that sits below its own format floor, cannot stand in the abstract in any form.

A4 -- a Section-3-conformant dense arm (prefill once per query, KV-cached decode) must be measured on the timing cohort, and the resulting comparison stated in whichever direction the data fall. The printed table implies the proposed operating point is dominated by the zero-storage endpoint on TTFT, F1 and Store; the paper cannot claim an interior point on a frontier while its own endpoint is mis-implemented.

A5 -- a quantized exact-cache baseline must appear, or its analytic byte count must be published and the headline restated against it. Omitting the cheapest competing capacity policy, buildable from the paper's own packer, is the central baseline failure for a capacity-first paper.

A3 -- the ForkAudit scope must be stated in the main text wherever ownership safety is claimed. Appendix disclosure on page 27 does not make the abstract, Figure 1 and contribution bullet 3 accurate for a reader of the nine-page submission.
A2 -- memory and quality must be quoted against a single reference arm, and the frozen-versus-full-prefix paired interval must be reported.

A6 -- the abstract's allocator result must be labelled as reproducing paged-prefix sharing against a controlled full-copy factor, with the peak figure and the audited fork's zero delta against the paper's own paged-prefix baseline stated where the claim is made.
A12 (LLM-use disclosure only) -- a venue compliance requirement, absent from all 31 pages.

capacity-first trade-off frontier between dense recompute and exact caching
issues.diagnosis: Every table's compression reference is an un-quantized cache. Table 1 rows: dense, full-prefix Q16/BF16 (136.235 MiB), split Q16 (34.683), frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 (9.661), same-memory mixed (9.395), aggressive mixed (7.536). Table 2 rows: dense, full-prefix Q16/BF16 (140.34), Q8 (15.89), Q4/Q4/Q8 (10.01), per-layer mixed (9.74), Q4 (8.41). Tables 18 and 19 add HYPIC and Radix prefix-cache arms, also un-quantized (139.53 MiB). No full-prefix Q8 or Q4 row exists anywhere in the paper. The quantizer in Sec 4.2 Eq. 3 is generic 64-value asymmetric min-max packing and is not specific to split state; the paper's own ratios show it delivers 34.683/9.661 = 3.59x, consistent with 4.5 effective bits per value. Applying the same 3.59x to the 136.235 MiB full-prefix entry gives roughly 38 MiB.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's central positioning claim is a location on a capacity-versus-latency frontier whose endpoints are dense recomputation and exact prefix caching (Sec 3, Sec 5.3, Conclusion). The most obvious intermediate point on that frontier - an exact prefix cache quantized with the paper's own quantizer - is absent. With that row present, the capacity advantage attributable to the split-replay design would fall from 14.1x to roughly 3.9x, and the comparison arm would retain the 0.163 s TTFT rather than paying 0.673 s. Since Sec 4.1 argues that a fair denominator must count the whole entry, applying the same standard to the baseline is the paper's own logic. As stated, the headline number credits to Q-CoMem a factor of about 3.6x that comes from quantization alone and is available to any caching scheme.
issues.required_action: Add full-prefix Q8 and full-prefix Q4/Q8 rows to Tables 1 and 2, quantized with the identical group-64 scheme and reported under the identical denominators, including their TTFT and F1 in Table 2. Restate the abstract, Sec 5.2, and the Conclusion so the headline compression factor is relative to the strongest equally-quantized exact cache, and report the un-quantized 14.10x only as a secondary reference.
issues.verification_test: Re-run Tables 1 and 2 with the added rows and check that the abstract's compression figure, Sec 5.2's text, and the Conclusion are all re-derived against the best quantized full-prefix row. A reviewer should be able to read the ratio 9.661 (or 10.01) divided by the quantized full-prefix Store directly off the table.
issues.evidence_required: Two additional configurations on each existing cohort using the already-implemented quantizer; no new method, model, or dataset is required.

But the projection holds only on the capacity axis: it assumes a quantized full-prefix arm suffers no additional quality loss from packing all ten attention layers' KV, which is exactly what is unmeasured. issues.location: Abstract (p.1, lines 022-026); Sec 1 contribution bullet 2 (p.2); Table 1 and its footnote (p.6); Sec 5.2 (p.6); Sec 5.4 (p.7); Conclusion (p.8)
issues.diagnosis: The headline row of Table 1 is quoted against three different reference arms in three different columns. The compression ratio (14.10x) is relative to full-prefix Q16/BF16 ('Compression is relative to full-prefix Q16/BF16', Table 1 footnote). The quality interval (-0.39 [-2.04, 1.08]) is relative to split Q16 ('intervals are paired 10,000-resample bootstrap intervals against split Q16'). The catastrophic-regression count (0/60) is relative to dense ('the registered per-item dF1-versus-dense <= -50 point rule'). The abstract, the contribution bullet, and the Conclusion all pair '14.10x smaller' with '-0.39 points' in one breath, so the two halves of the paper's single most-quoted sentence are measured against different baselines. The comparison a deployment decision actually turns on, frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 versus full-prefix Q16, has point estimate 54.24 - 54.68 = -0.44 and appears nowhere: not in Table 1, not in Sec 5.4, and not in the artifact claim text (C-QCOMEM-60-STORE-F1-01 reports only the Q16-split-relative delta -0.003870 with interval [-0.020365, 0.010756]).
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's thesis is a trade-off between a memory number and a quality number. If those two numbers are computed against different arms, the trade-off as stated does not correspond to any single decision a reader can make. A practitioner is choosing between exact prefix caching (136.235 MiB) and Q-CoMem (9.661 MiB); the quality cost of that choice is -0.44 with an unreported interval, not -0.39 against an intermediate configuration that nobody would deploy. Table 1's own full-prefix row (+0.06 [0.00, 0.18] versus split Q16) shows the split step itself carries a small, essentially always-nonnegative quality cost, so the two deltas compound rather than cancel. This is the difference between a correctly stated trade-off and a favorably assembled one.
issues.required_action: Report the frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 versus full-prefix Q16 paired difference and its 95% bootstrap interval, and make the abstract, contribution bullet, Sec 5.2, Sec 5.4, and Conclusion quote memory and quality against the same arm (full-prefix Q16). Either add a second dF1 column to Table 1 with full-prefix as reference, or change the existing column's reference arm and keep the split-Q16 comparison as an ablation row. Use one reference arm for the catastrophic-regression rule as well, or state explicitly in the main text that the safety rule uses a third arm.
issues.verification_test: Recompute from the 360 archived item-level F1 values in E-QCOMEM-60-VALIDATION-20260812D-A the paired per-item deltas of frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 minus full-prefix Q16 and their 10,000-resample paired bootstrap interval. Check that the reported point estimate equals 54.2368 - 54.6800 to three decimals, that Table 1's dF1 column header names the same arm as the compression column, and that a text search for '14.10' and '-0.39' returns no sentence in which the two are paired against different references.
issues.evidence_required: One re-analysis of already-archived item-level F1 data; no new GPU execution required.
issues.meta_reason: Adjudicated as actionable and folded into A2.

issues.location: Section 5.5 'Ownership-audit cohort and procedure' (p.7, lines 363-368); Table 3 (p.14); Section 3 third paragraph (p.3-4); Sections 4.3-4.4 (p.5); Abstract (p.1); Appendix H (p.27)
issues.diagnosis: Section 5.5 states the audited configuration is 'ten vLLM-0.26 Triton full-attention layers with BF16 KV (the protocol's "Q16" storage label, not quantization) and 128-token pages, plus thirty Transformers-torch GDN layers', with PG-19 4,095-token documents, a 32-token registered transition, N in {1,8,32}, and 8 argmax outputs. Table 3 confirms: 'KV backend: vLLM fused attention; BF16/Q16; page 128' and 'Document / query: 4,095 / 32 tokens; PG-19 train only'. Nothing in Section 5.5 or Table 3 mentions a split depth j, a boundary residual, a dequantization step, or Qasper/2WikiMQA. By contrast Tables 1 and 2 measure a j=7 quantized Q4/Q4/Q8 split-replay path on Qasper/2WikiMQA under Transformers. The only signal that these differ is Appendix H's phrase 'one page size, 16-bit KV', 27 pages in. Meanwhile the abstract asserts 'A fail-closed FORKAUDIT trace validates immutability, copy-on-write, recurrent rebinding, and call provenance' immediately after describing the Q-CoMem Read path, and Section 3's third paragraph presents hybrid mutability as the reason Sections 4.3 and 4.4 exist.
issues.why_it_matters: This is precisely the structural failure my lens is asked to test for. The paper's argument is Motivation (retained state is the controllable term; the hybrid entry is mutable, so sharing is an ownership question) -> Methodology (Section 4.3 forks the dequantized entry under an ownership discipline; Section 4.4 validates that discipline) -> Experiments (Section 5.5 reports whether the discipline holds). The first two links hold. The third does not: Section 5.5 tests a different artifact from the one Section 4.3 describes and from the one Sections 5.2-5.4 measure. So the Experiments section is not one story with the Methodology - it is two, and the seam is invisible unless the reader collates a sentence on p.7 with a table on p.14 and a clause on p.27. Because the abstract and Section 1's third contribution bullet couple ForkAudit to Q-CoMem without qualification, a reader will reasonably conclude the shipped quantized path has been ownership-audited. On the evidence in this PDF, it has not.
issues.required_action: State the scope gap explicitly in three places. (1) In Section 5.1, add a short table or paragraph mapping each results table (1, 2, 15) to the exact executed system: model, runtime, KV backend, split depth, quantization policy, dataset. (2) In Section 5.5's first sentence, say plainly that the primary factorial runs BF16/Q16 KV with no split residual and therefore audits the ownership discipline, not the quantized Read path. (3) In the abstract, either qualify the ForkAudit sentence ('on a BF16-KV configuration of the same ownership design') or, preferably, run the seven-target contract on the Q4/Q4/Q8 configuration of Table 1 and report that verdict. Add the gap to Section 5.6 as a named limitation.
issues.verification_test: Hand the revised main text to a reader who has not seen the appendix and ask: 'Was the Q4/Q4/Q8 configuration reported in Table 1 ever passed through ForkAudit, yes or no?' The revision passes only if the reader answers correctly from Sections 5.1-5.5 alone, without consulting Table 3 or Appendix H. Additionally, a diff of the stated configurations for Table 1, Table 2 and Table 15 should surface every axis on which they differ.
issues.evidence_required: Either a ForkAudit execution on the quantized split-replay Read path with the seven-target coverage/verdict table for that exact configuration, or an explicit, prominently placed statement that the quantized path is unaudited and that the ownership result transfers only by design argument.

issues.location: Table 2 (p.6) 'No-cache dense recompute' row; Section 5.3 (p.6); Section 3 (p.3) 'Dense recomputation sets S(D) = 0 but pays full prefill on every query'; Appendix Table 18 (p.24) and Table 19 (p.25)
issues.diagnosis: Table 2's dense arm reports TTFT 0.649 s and TPOT 648.75 ms. These differ by 0.04%, i.e. every decoded token costs another full prefill; no other row in the paper has TPOT above 55.5 ms on the same model and hardware. I verified the table is otherwise internally exact: tok/s = n/(TTFT + n*TPOT) with n = 8 reproduces all six reported throughputs (dense 1.370 vs 1.36; full-prefix 13.426 vs 13.38; Q8 7.165 vs 7.15; Q4/Q4/Q8 7.183 vs 7.19; per-layer 7.184 vs 7.19; Q4 7.180 vs 7.19), which confirms 648.75 ms really is a per-decode-step cost and not an aggregate. Section 3 defines the dense endpoint differently, as paying full prefill 'on every query'. Substituting the full-prefix decode cost (54.11 ms) into a Section-3-conformant dense arm gives 8 tokens in 0.649 + 8(0.05411) = 1.082 s = 7.40 tok/s, against Q-CoMem's measured 1.113 s = 7.19 tok/s. That arm also has Store 0.00 MiB (vs 10.01) and the best F1 in the table (39.42 vs 39.01). The paper's own Appendix Table 19 corroborates this: SGLang 0.5.17 with prefix reuse OFF - a genuine no-document-cache baseline - records TTFT 0.283 s, TPOT 53.38 ms, 12.73 tok/s and F1 39.14 on the identical eight items and hardware.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's entire thesis is that Q-CoMem buys a smaller S(D) by spending online work, i.e. that it occupies a useful interior point between dense recomputation (S(D)=0) and exact prefix caching. If the dense endpoint as defined in Section 3 is faster than Q-CoMem while retaining nothing, then Q-CoMem is Pareto-dominated at that end and the interior point does not exist. On the numbers as printed, the only axis on which Q-CoMem beats dense is TPOT/throughput, and that margin rests entirely on a dense row that recomputes the prefix at every token. This is not a presentational quibble: it decides whether the contribution is a trade-off or a dominated design. It also cannot be waved off as a runtime-mismatch artifact, because Table 19's within-paper SGLang-cache-off row shows the same qualitative conclusion on the same slice with an off-the-shelf framework.
issues.required_action: Add to the Table 2 block a dense arm that prefills once per query and decodes with a standard KV cache, matched in stack and harness to the Q-CoMem rows, and report its TTFT, TPOT, throughput, F1 and Store alongside them. State explicitly in Section 5.1 what caching the 'no-cache' arm does and does not use, and reconcile it with the Section 3 definition. If the Section-3-conformant dense arm dominates Q-CoMem on this workload, say so and restate the contribution as bounded to the regime where it does not (e.g. deeper j, longer generations, or many-document residency where 140 MiB/doc of full-prefix cache is the binding constraint and dense prefill latency is unacceptable).
issues.verification_test: Re-run the eight indices-6-9 items with three configurations under one harness: (a) prefill-per-query dense with decode KV cache, (b) full-prefix Q16 reuse, (c) Q-CoMem frozen Q4/Q4/Q8. Report per-item generated-token count, TTFT, per-step decode latency, end-to-end wall time and F1. The paper's claim survives only if (c) beats (a) on end-to-end latency or throughput at equal or better F1, or if the authors instead demonstrate a residency regime (documents per device at fixed VRAM) in which (a) is infeasible. Additionally check that a single-query end-to-end latency curve versus number of generated tokens crosses in favour of (c) somewhere within a realistic generation length.
issues.evidence_required: A matched dense-with-decode-cache row in Table 2; per-item raw timing traces including generated-token counts; and either a crossover analysis versus generation length or a documents-per-device capacity measurement at fixed VRAM that shows what the retained entry actually buys.
issues.meta_reason: Adjudicated as actionable and folded into A4.

issues.location: Sec 5.5 p.7 (lines 363-366); contribution bullet 3 p.2 (lines 095-098); Figure 1 p.2; Table 5 p.16; Appendix H p.27 (line 1437)
issues.diagnosis: Sec 5.5 states the ownership cohort is 'ten vLLM-0.26 Triton full-attention layers with BF16 KV (the protocol's "Q16" storage label, not quantization) and 128-token pages, plus thirty Transformers-torch GDN layers', driven by PG-19 books. Appendix H confirms 'The primary factorial covers one model, one H20 hardware family, one page size, 16-bit KV, and N <= 32.' The deployment cohorts (Tables 1 and 2) are in-process Transformers with packed Q4/Q8 state on Qasper/2WikiMQA. Table 5's cohort-to-claim map lists no cell whose frozen scope includes quantized state. So no ForkAudit cell exercises the dequantize-then-fork Read path that Sec 4.3 and Figure 1 describe.
issues.why_it_matters: Contribution bullet 3 and Figure 1's single unified geometry present ForkAudit as the validation rail of the Q-CoMem Read path, and the abstract states the audit 'validates immutability, copy-on-write, recurrent rebinding, and call provenance' as part of the Q-CoMem design. What was actually audited is an un-quantized adapter on a different dataset and runtime. This matters mechanically, not just rhetorically: Read dequantizes packed entries into fresh BF16 tensors per request, which changes which tensors can be aliased, which must be copied on write, and where a rebind is required - precisely the structure the seven targets check. The paper's most rigorous evidence therefore does not attach to the system the paper is about. Appendix H discloses the precision, but a reader who stops at the main text will reasonably conclude otherwise.
issues.required_action: Either run at least one ForkAudit factorial cell on the packed Q4/Q8 Read path and report the seven-target verdict, or state plainly in Sec 5.5, in contribution bullet 3, and in Figure 1's caption that the ownership audit covers a BF16-KV adapter and that ownership on the quantized path is unvalidated. Add an explicit exclusion to the corresponding Table 5 row.
issues.verification_test: Search the revised main text for a sentence naming the audited state precision at the point where 'ownership-safe reuse' is claimed. If a quantized cell was added, Table 6 must carry its coverage and verdict; if not, Table 5's primary-factorial row must list 'quantized Read path' among its explicit exclusions.
issues.evidence_required: One additional factorial cell with packed state, or a scope amendment; the latter costs nothing.

issues.location: Abstract p.1 (lines 031-032); contribution bullet 3 p.2 (lines 097-098); Sec 5.5 'Allocator reduction' p.8 (lines 404-410); Table 15 p.21; Appendix H p.27

54.5% allocator reduction relative to full-copy KV

issues.why_it_matters: Sharing one document's KV across concurrent requests instead of copying it per request is the core of PagedAttention (2023), which this paper cites and builds on. This is the clearest instance in the paper of a claim boundary being inflated, and it is out of keeping with the care shown elsewhere.

issues.location: Table 1 p.6 (dense 54.29, delta -0.33 [-4.61, 2.67]; full-prefix Q16 54.68, delta +0.06 [0.00, 0.18]); Sec 5.1 p.5-6; Table 18 footnote p.24
claim_ids: mean F1 difference of -0.39 [-2.04, 1.08] versus split Q16
dense recomputation and exact prefix caching are the two endpoints
issues.diagnosis: Exact prefix caching is mathematically equivalent to dense recomputation modulo numerics, so both should give near-identical per-item F1 and near-identical paired intervals against split Q16. Table 1 instead shows full-prefix Q16 nearly item-identical to split Q16 (paired CI [0.00, 0.18], width 0.18) while dense recomputation is far from it (paired CI [-4.61, 2.67], width 7.28). The only explanation I could find is a footnote to Table 18 on p.24: 'Full-prefix Q16 is CoMem's matched semantic comparator; no-cache recompute uses a different document/query execution boundary.' Nothing in Sec 5.1, Sec 5.2, or Sec 5.4 says this, and the difference is never quantified.
issues.why_it_matters: Sec 3 builds the entire motivation on dense recomputation and exact prefix caching as the two endpoints of the trade-off. If the dense arm runs a materially different prompt/execution boundary, it is not a valid endpoint and the reader cannot interpret its row. Symmetrically, the near-identity between full-prefix Q16 and split Q16 becomes the surprising fact, and it is the reference against which the -0.39 headline delta is computed. A reader assessing whether the headline quality claim is meaningful needs to know which arm is the semantically matched comparator and by how much the other differs.
issues.required_action: Define both endpoints' document/query execution boundary explicitly in Sec 5.1, promote the Table 18 footnote's content into the main text, and report the direct paired per-item difference between dense recomputation and full-prefix Q16 with a bootstrap interval.
issues.verification_test: Add a dense-versus-full-prefix paired difference row with a 95% bootstrap interval. If it is not centered near zero with a narrow interval, the manuscript must state why exact caching is not reproducing dense recomputation on this stack.
issues.evidence_required: One additional paired comparison computed from the already-archived per-item F1 values (the reproducibility statement says all 360 item-level F1 values replay).

issues.location: Table 1 (p.6) and Table 2 (p.7) row sets; Sec 2 'Hybrid state and cache management' (p.3); Sec 5.1 (p.5-6)
issues.diagnosis: The evaluated policy set in both tables varies only along the split-replay axis: dense, full-prefix Q16/BF16, split Q16/BF16, frozen Q4/Q4/Q8, and two mixed policies (Table 1); dense, full-prefix Q16/BF16, Q8, Q4/Q4/Q8, per-layer mixed, Q4 (Table 2). There is no quantized full-prefix row anywhere. The 14.10x headline is therefore measured entirely against an unquantized BF16 cache. The paper is aware of the competing literature (Palu, SqueezeAttention, HeadKV cited in Sec 2, p.3) and even ports Palu in a bounded operator study (Table 17, p.23), but never applies its own Eq. 3 groupwise packer to the full-prefix KV, which is a few lines of code given that the packer already exists and already runs on lower-layer KV.
issues.why_it_matters: For a paper whose single claim is capacity, the strongest and cheapest competing capacity policy has been omitted. Quantizing the full-prefix KV to Q4 with the paper's own packer should give roughly 4x on 136.235 MiB (about 34 MiB) at essentially unchanged TTFT and without any suffix reconstruction. That would make the honest advantage of split replay approximately 3.5x rather than 14.10x, at the cost of a 4x TTFT regression and a throughput halving. A reader cannot tell from this paper whether split replay is needed at all to reach the capacity goal, or whether the quantizer alone does most of the work. That is precisely the question the paper's own two-factor decomposition (splitting 3.93x, quantization 3.59x) invites and then leaves unanswered from the other direction.
issues.required_action: Add 'full-prefix Q8' and 'full-prefix Q4' rows to Table 1 and Table 2, produced with the same Eq. 3 packer, the same cohorts, and the same denominators as the existing rows, and report the frozen policy's compression ratio and paired F1 interval relative to the best quantized full-prefix point in addition to the BF16 reference. If quantized full-prefix is infeasible in this implementation, say so explicitly and give the analytic byte count so the comparison can still be made.
issues.verification_test: Run the existing packer over the full-prefix KV on the 60-item cohort and record Store and F1 under the Table 1 component accounting. Require that the reported headline compression is restated relative to the best quantized full-prefix row, and that the paired bootstrap interval of frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 versus that row is reported. Cross-check the analytic expectation: full-prefix Q4 Store should land near 136.235/4 plus group scale/bias overhead.
issues.evidence_required: One additional 60-item run (and ideally one 8-item timing run) of an existing code path over already-frozen inputs.
issues.meta_reason: The byte arithmetic is correct and I reproduce it: at 4.5 effective bits per value, full-prefix Q4 is 136.235 x 36/128 = 38.3 MiB, giving 3.97x over the printed 9.661 (and 3.30x over a floor-respecting ~11.6 MiB); a Q4/Q4/Q8-style full-prefix entry is ~45.6 MiB, giving 4.72x. But the projection holds only on the capacity axis: it assumes a quantized full-prefix arm suffers no additional quality loss from packing all ten attention layers' KV, which is exactly what is unmeasured. The missing-baseline demand survives in full; the numerical conclusion 'the advantage is only ~3.9x' survives only as a capacity-axis estimate and must not be stated as the corrected headline until the arm is actually run or its F1 bounded.

issues.location: Table 2 rows 1 and 3-6 (p.7); Sec 5.3 (p.6-7); Abstract (p.1, lines 027-030)
issues.diagnosis: In the paper's own Table 2, no-cache dense recompute records TTFT 0.649 s while every Q-CoMem row records 0.673-0.674 s. Sec 5.3 discusses dense only through its TPOT ('dense recomputation has 648.75 ms TPOT') and never states the TTFT comparison; the abstract compares Q-CoMem's TTFT only with full-prefix Q16 ('full-prefix Q16 is faster (0.163 versus about 0.673 s)'). Its genuine advantage over dense is confined to TPOT (55 vs 649 ms) and throughput (7.19 vs 1.36 tok/s), and those depend on how the dense arm is implemented (see R44-4-12). Omitting an adverse comparison that is visible in one's own table, while stating the other adverse comparison, is selective reporting even when unintentional, and it is the kind of omission that a rigor reviewer must flag.

Adjust the Sec 3 and Figure 1 'between the endpoints' framing to say that the interpolation is in retained bytes, not in first-token latency.

issues.location: Abstract (p.1, lines 031-032); Sec 1 contribution bullet 3 (p.2); Sec 5.5 'Allocator reduction with canonical equality' (p.7); Table 15 (p.21); Appendix H (p.27)
issues.diagnosis: The abstract and contribution bullet 3 headline a 54.5% post-priming allocator reduction at N=32 (4.901 -> 2.229 GiB) against a full-copy KV control. Appendix H (p.27) states that 'Full-copy KV and materialized GDN bases are controlled ownership factors rather than optimized production baselines'. Table 15 itself labels 'Shared-doc KV / Materialized GDN base' as the 'Paged-prefix baseline' and shows it at 2.229 GiB final and 2.843 GiB peak, identical to the 'Audited hybrid fork' row (2.229 / 2.843), with the audited fork worse on generation increment (1.950 vs 0.019 GiB). Separately, the abstract and main text report the final allocated delta (54.5%) but never the peak reduction, which from the same table is 1 - 2.843/4.920 = 42.2%.

First, the headline percentage is measured against a control the authors themselves say is not an optimized baseline, while against the paper's own paged-prefix baseline the audited ownership mechanism yields exactly zero allocator benefit at both final and peak, and a worse generation increment. Second, in a capacity-first paper, peak allocation is the quantity that determines OOM and admission, and the paper reports the metric with the larger reduction (final, 54.5%) in the abstract while the smaller and more deployment-relevant one (peak, 42.2%) appears only in an appendix table. A reader of the abstract will attribute the 54.5% to the paper's contribution; Table 15 says it belongs to shared-document KV, which is what PagedAttention already does.
issues.required_action: In the abstract and contributions, report the allocator result against both arms: the 54.5% versus the full-copy control and the 0% versus the paper's own paged-prefix baseline, and label the full-copy arm as a controlled factor rather than a baseline at first mention. Report peak alongside final in the main text, and state the generation-increment cost of borrowed GDN (1.950 vs 0.019 GiB) where the result is first claimed rather than only in Table 15.
issues.verification_test: Confirm from Table 15 that shared-doc/materialized and shared-doc/borrowed both read 2.229 final and 2.843 peak, and that the abstract's percentage is accompanied by the paged-prefix comparison. Recompute 1 - 2.843/4.920 = 42.2% and require the peak figure to appear wherever 54.5% appears.

issues.location: Eq. 2 and Sec. 4.1 (p.4); Sec. 4.2 (p.4); Table 2 footnote (p.7); Table 18 footnote (p.24); Table 3 (p.14)
issues.diagnosis: Two problems make Eq. 2 non-instantiable. First, the model geometry needed to evaluate it is never given: Table 3 states only 'Qwen3.5-35B-A3B; 10 attention + 30 GDN layers', and no hidden size, KV head count, head dimension, GDN convolution width, or recurrent state shape appears anywhere in the paper. A reader therefore cannot derive any term of S_QCoMem(D; j, b), cannot check that 136.235 -> 34.683 is consistent with removing all but one lower attention layer, and cannot predict Store for any other depth or model. Second, the per-layer policy retains a component that Eq. 2 does not contain: Sec. 4.2 says 'the reported per-layer policy uses a Q4 residual, Q16 projections, and active-layer widths [8, 8, 4, 4, 8, 8, 8]', and both Table 2's and Table 18's footnotes repeat 'Q4 residual, Q16 projections'. Eq. 2 has exactly three terms - residual, lower KV, lower convolution/recurrent state - and 'projections' is defined nowhere in the paper. That row's Store (9.74 MiB in Table 2, 9.395 MiB as 'same-memory mixed' in Table 1) therefore cannot be reconstructed from the paper's own decomposition. The naming also shifts between tables: the same policy is 'same-memory mixed' in Table 1, 'per-layer mixed' in Table 2, and 'CoMem per-layer mixed' in Table 18.
issues.why_it_matters: Eq. 2 is the paper's formal statement of what it contributes - counting the whole entry rather than the residual alone. If the equation cannot be evaluated for the reported model and does not cover the components an evaluated policy actually retains, then the central accounting claim is not independently checkable and the ablation rows are not reproducible. This is the analytical counterpart of issue R44-5-05: neither the empirical nor the analytical route to Store is open to a reader.
issues.required_action: Add a small table giving, for the evaluated configuration, the per-component retained tensor shapes and byte counts at BF16 and under each policy, so that the six Store values in Table 1 follow arithmetically from Eq. 2. Either add the projection term to Eq. 2 with a definition, or remove 'Q16 projections' from the policy descriptions. Use one name per policy across all tables.
issues.verification_test: From the published shapes and bit assignments, recompute S_QCoMem for full-prefix Q16, split Q16, frozen Q4/Q4/Q8, per-layer mixed, and aggressive mixed, and confirm agreement with 136.235, 34.683, 9.661, 9.395, and 7.536 MiB/doc within the stated group/metadata overhead.
issues.evidence_required: Retained tensor shape/dtype inventory for one document entry, and a definition of the 'projections' component.
issues.meta_reason: Adjudicated as actionable and folded into A1.

issues.location: Table 2 dense row (p.7); Sec. 5.3 (pp.6-7); Table 1 caption catastrophic-regression rule (p.6); Table 18 footnote (p.24)
issues.diagnosis: The 'no-cache dense recompute' arm is never operationally defined, and its reported numbers imply an unusual configuration. Table 2 gives dense TTFT = 0.649 s and TPOT = 648.75 ms - equal to within 0.04% - which is the signature of re-running the full prefix at every decode step rather than prefilling once and decoding from a KV cache. Sec. 5.3 quotes this as a result ('dense recomputation has 648.75 ms TPOT'). The paper's only characterisations are Sec. 3's 'stores no document state but repeatedly processes the prefix' and Table 18's footnote 'no-cache recompute uses a different document/query execution boundary', neither of which says what happens during decoding. The definition is load-bearing beyond the timing table: Table 1's caption defines the registered catastrophic-regression rule as 'per-item Delta-F1-versus-dense <= -50 point', so the dense arm is the reference for a reported 0/60, 1/60, and 5/60 failure count.

Because the same arm defines the catastrophic-regression baseline, an unstated difference in its execution boundary also touches the quality claims.
issues.required_action: Define the dense arm precisely: whether the document is re-prefilled per query or per token, whether a KV cache is retained during decoding, and what the 'different document/query execution boundary' consists of. If it recomputes per token, add a standard cached-prefill dense arm and report both.
issues.verification_test: Instrument the dense arm to count forward passes over the document per query; confirm the count is 1 for a cached-prefill implementation, and report TTFT, TPOT, and tok/s for that implementation next to the current row.
issues.evidence_required: The dense-arm execution configuration and per-query forward-pass counts.

issues.location: Abstract (p.1, lines 031-033); Section 5.5 'Allocator reduction with canonical equality' (p.8); Table 15 (p.22); Section 2 'Paged and prefix-aware inference' (p.3)
issues.diagnosis: The abstract states 'Separately, shared-document KV lowers the post-priming allocated delta from 4.901 to 2.229 GiB at N = 32'. Table 15 shows the four endpoints: Full-copy KV/Materialized GDN = 4.901, Full-copy KV/Borrowed GDN = 4.890, Shared-doc KV/Materialized GDN ('Paged-prefix baseline') = 2.229, Shared-doc KV/Borrowed GDN ('Audited hybrid fork') = 2.229. Final and Peak are identical (2.229 / 2.843) for the last two rows; only the generation increment differs (0.019 vs 1.950), which Section 5.5 correctly characterizes as an allocation-timing change. So the entire 54.5% reduction is produced by KV block sharing, which the paper itself attributes to PagedAttention in Section 2, and the borrowed-GDN ownership mechanism - the actually novel part - contributes nothing to the final or peak allocator figure.
issues.why_it_matters: This number is one of four quantitative results in the abstract, sits immediately beside the paper's own contributions, and is the only GiB-scale figure in the paper. The word 'Separately' is the sole cue that it does not come from Q-CoMem's novel mechanism. The paper's technical statements are accurate and its Table 15 is honest, but the abstract's placement invites exactly the misattribution the rest of the paper works hard to prevent, and it inflates the apparent contribution relative to what the ownership design itself buys.
issues.required_action: In the abstract, attribute the reduction to KV block sharing explicitly and note that it is measured under a third denominator distinct from Store. In Section 5.5, add one sentence stating what the borrowed-GDN arm contributes on its own (per Table 15: no change in final or peak allocated bytes; a shift of ~1.93 GiB of allocation from setup to generation time), so the reader sees the ownership mechanism's own allocator cost-benefit rather than only the shared-KV headline.
issues.verification_test: Read the abstract's four quantitative claims and ask, for each, 'which mechanism in this paper produced it?' Every answer must be unambiguous from the abstract sentence alone. The 54.5% claim currently fails this test.

issues.location: Table 1 (p.6), rows 'Q-CoMem frozen Q4/Q4/Q8' (9.661 MiB, 14.10x) and 'Q-CoMem same-memory mixed' (9.395 MiB); against Eq. 3 and Figure 2c (p.4) and Section 5.1 'Memory denominators' (p.5); abstract (p.1); Section 5.2 (p.6); Section 6 (p.9)
issues.diagnosis: Eq. 3 with Figure 2c's stated format - 64 values per group, packed unsigned b-bit codes, BF16 scale and BF16 bias - gives per-group sizes of 36 bytes at Q4 and 68 bytes at Q8 against 128 bytes at BF16, i.e. maximum compression 3.5556x (Q4) and 1.8824x (Q8). Table 1 requires 34.683 -> 9.661 MiB, a ratio of 3.590x, for a policy that packs GDN state at Q8. Even setting the Q8 GDN component to exactly zero, the pure-Q4 floor is 34.683 * 36/128 = 9.755 MiB, above the reported 9.661; the same-memory mixed row (9.395) is further below the floor. Using the GDN share I recovered from Table 2 (6.40 of 29.90 MiB, 21.4%), the frozen policy should land at 11.61 MiB, i.e. 11.73x rather than 14.10x. Table 2 is not affected: the same model reproduces its Q8, Q4, Q4/Q4/Q8 and per-layer rows to within 0.03% from a common 29.90 MiB BF16 entry, which is strong evidence that the packing model is correct and that the 60-item panel's component accounting is the outlier. Section 5.1 does say the two panels use different Store implementations, but a different summation cannot place a quantized entry below the byte floor of its own format.
issues.why_it_matters: 14.10x is the paper's headline number - it appears in the abstract, in contribution bullet 2, in Section 5.2 and in the conclusion - and it is the product of the 3.93x split factor and the disputed 3.59x quantization factor. If the quantization factor is capped at 3.5556x and is realistically nearer 3.0x once Q8 GDN state is counted, the headline drops to roughly 12x. A reviewer cannot reconstruct the paper's central quantity from the paper's own method section, which is exactly the check Eq. 2 and Eq. 3 exist to enable.
issues.required_action: Publish, for every Table 1 row, the byte breakdown into packed residual codes, residual scales, residual biases, lower attention KV codes plus metadata, and lower GDN codes plus metadata, and show that each row satisfies sum over components of ceil(n_values/64) * (b*64/8 + 4) bytes. Report both panels under one accounting implementation as the primary result.
issues.verification_test: Instrument the 60-item Store accountant to emit component-level byte counts per item and per policy, then assert programmatically that the packed size of each component equals ceil(n/64)*(b*8 + 4) bytes and that split-Q16-size / frozen-size <= 3.5556. Independently, recompute Table 1's Store with the Table 2 byte-range-union accountant on the same 60 items and report both columns side by side; the two should agree to within the metadata the paper says it excludes.
issues.evidence_required: Per-component byte tables for all Table 1 rows, the group-size and metadata dtype actually used by the 60-item packer, and a cross-accountant comparison of the two Store implementations on a common item set.
issues.meta_reason: The unconditional part survives and I confirm it: 9.661 MiB is below the 9.755 MiB pure-Q4 format floor implied by Eq. 3 and Figure 2c. The specific corrected value does not: it imports the GDN share (21.4%) recovered from Table 2's byte-range-union accounting into Table 1's component accounting, and Section 5.1 states those implementations differ. The authors must publish the component breakdown; they must not be required to print 11.73x.

issues.location: Abstract (p.1); Figure 1 audit rail (p.2); Section 4.4 (p.5) 'ForkAudit validates the Section 4.3 lifecycle'; Section 5 intro (p.5); Section 5.5 (p.7); Appendix Table 3 (p.14) and Table 5 (p.14-16)
issues.diagnosis: Table 3 pins the primary factorial to: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B with all 10 attention plus all 30 GDN layers, vLLM fused attention with BF16/Q16 KV at page 128, 4,095-token PG-19 documents, 32-token transition, 8 output tokens. issues.location: Abstract (p.1, lines 032-034); Sec 1 (p.1-2); Sec 3 (p.3); Sec 5.5 'Falsification beyond output equality' (p.7); Table 14 'Base inv.' column (p.21); Appendix H (p.29)

issues.location: Sec 4.1 (p.4); Figure 2 caption (p.4); Sec 5.1 (p.5-6); Tables 1 and 2 (pp.6-7)

Sec 4.1 identifies the bit vector b as 'the design surface' and every one of the six evaluated points in Table 1 and six in Table 2 varies only bit widths. Yet Eq. 2 makes S(D) an explicit function of j: the number of retained lower-layer KV and recurrent sidecars grows with j while the residual term does not, and Sec 3 describes split replay as sitting between the endpoints precisely as a function of depth.

Without any depth variation the paper reports six points on a one-dimensional slice of a two-dimensional design space and cannot claim to have characterized the frontier it motivates. A depth sweep might also address R44-4-04, since a shallower split would reduce suffix reconstruction cost and hence TTFT.

issues.location: Table 1 footnote (p.6); Sec 5.4 (p.7); Reproducibility Statement (p.9)
issues.diagnosis: The Reproducibility Statement (p.9) and Appendix A (p.12) state that 24 paired-bootstrap intervals were computed; Table 1 displays five. The paper does not say which 24, how the displayed five were chosen, or whether any multiplicity consideration applies. The registered catastrophic-regression rule uses a threshold of -50 F1 points (equivalently -0.5 on the [0,1] scale) against dense, under which the frozen policy scores 0/60; a -50-point per-item threshold on a 0-100 scale only fires on near-total answer failure.
issues.why_it_matters: Reporting five of twenty-four intervals without stating the selection rule leaves open whether the displayed set is the complete set for the compared policies or a chosen subset, which matters because the headline interval is the one that crosses zero. Separately, '0/60 catastrophic regressions' reads as a per-item safety guarantee but, at a -50-point threshold, is close to vacuous; a more informative per-item regression rate at a threshold such as -10 points would say something a reader can use, and can be computed from the archived item-level data at no cost.
issues.required_action: State how many intervals were computed, which policies and reference arms they cover, and how the displayed subset was chosen; report all of them in an appendix table. Add a per-item regression rate at a substantively meaningful threshold alongside the -50-point registered rule, and use a single reference arm consistent with R44-4-01.
issues.verification_test: Require the appendix to list all 24 intervals with their reference arms, and require the per-item delta distribution (or at minimum the count of items below -10 points) for each policy, recomputed from the 360 archived item-level F1 values.
issues.evidence_required: Re-analysis of archived item-level data only.
issues.meta_reason: The threshold was preregistered and reporting 0/60 against it is exactly the right behaviour; re-characterising a preregistered rule after seeing the result is not a defect finding. The constructive half of the issue is accepted: state how many of the 24 computed intervals are displayed and why, and add a per-item regression rate at a substantively informative threshold alongside -- not instead of -- the registered rule.

issues.location: Eq. 4 (p.5) against Eq. 2 (p.4); Eq. 5 (p.5)
issues.diagnosis: Eq. 2 sums over l < j, l in A and l < j, l in G. Eq. 4 defines the fork as ({K_l^D, K_l^r}_{l in A}, {G_l^D, G_l^r}_{l in G}) with no l < j restriction, so as written it forks document state at every attention and recurrent layer, contradicting Figure 2a's 'No upper-suffix document state is retained'. Eq. 4 also has no r-dependence on its right-hand side beyond a superscript label, so F_1(D) and F_2(D) are syntactically identical, and it encodes none of the immutability, copy-on-write, rebinding or temporal semantics that the surrounding two sentences actually carry. In Eq. 5, the mandatory-slot family M_i(Sigma) is introduced in the preceding line and then never appears in the formula (presumably absorbed into Coverage_i), leaving dangling notation in the paper's central definition.
issues.why_it_matters: The ownership contract is the paper's main formal object, and neither of the two equations that state it carries the content. A reader checking whether the contract is well defined - the exact question a soundness reviewer must answer - finds that the definitions delegate everything to prose. The l < j discrepancy is a straightforward error that also confuses what is retained.
issues.required_action: Restrict Eq. 4's index sets to l < j. Replace the set-builder with an ownership-typed definition: give each coordinate an owner tag and a phase index, define share, copy-on-write and rebind as transitions over (owner, storage) pairs, and state the invariant that must hold at setup, transition and final. In Eq. 5, either use M_i(Sigma) explicitly (e.g. Coverage_i(tau) = complete iff every slot in M_i(Sigma) is present, unique and bound) or drop the symbol.
issues.verification_test: Check that the revised Eq. 4 instantiated at j = 7 with A = {3}, G = {0,1,2,4,5,6} yields exactly the tensor set counted by Eq. 2, and that each of the seven ForkAudit targets in Table 6 maps to a named clause of the revised definition.
issues.evidence_required: None beyond a corrected formalization.
issues.meta_reason: Adjudicated as actionable and folded into A12.

issues.location: Eq. 3 (p.4); Figure 2c (p.4); Eq. 6 (p.18)
issues.diagnosis: Eq. 3 sets s = (u - m)/(2^b - 1) and q = clip(round((x - m)/s), 0, 2^b - 1). For a constant group u = m gives s = 0 and the map is undefined; the paper specifies no epsilon, no fallback and no convention. The dequantization map (presumably x_hat = m + s*q) is never written, so the reconstruction error model is unstated. In Eq. 6, d_i = (s_i - 1) t_i is computed per dimension; for an empty dimension s_i = 0 this yields d_i = -t_i, which pushes m below the storage offset and can make the interval start negative, tripping the paper's own non-negativity requirement on a legitimately empty view.
issues.why_it_matters: Eq. 3 is the paper's only statement of what the quantizer does, and it is one of the two equations a reader must use to reproduce the Store column (see T-02). Degenerate groups are common in recurrent and convolution state (zero-initialized or saturated channels), so the s = 0 case is not hypothetical. The Eq. 6 edge case is minor but it sits inside the audit's soundness argument.
issues.required_action: Define the s = 0 case explicitly (e.g. s := 1 and q := 0, reconstructing exactly m) and give the dequantization formula. Guard Eq. 6 with d_i := 0 when s_i = 0, or state that empty views are excluded from the witness.
issues.verification_test: Unit-test the packer on constant groups, single-element groups and empty tensors, asserting exact round-trip for constant groups and a well-formed empty interval; assert that the packed byte count matches ceil(n/64)*(b*8 + 4) in every case.
issues.evidence_required: The implemented degenerate-case convention and its round-trip test.
issues.meta_reason: Adjudicated as actionable and folded into A12.

issues.location: Section 5.4 (p.6) 'We therefore use frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 as the headline operating point'; Table 1 CI column (p.6); abstract (p.1)
issues.diagnosis: Six retention policies are compared against split Q16 with six paired bootstrap intervals on the same 60-item validation panel, with no multiplicity adjustment, and the headline point is then chosen in Section 5.4 by comparing those same validation results ('the two mixed policies are ablations... We therefore use frozen Q4/Q4/Q8'). Section 4.2 states that the per-layer bit vector was calibrated on four disjoint items, but the choice of which policy to headline is not protected by that calibration set. The reported -0.39 [-2.04, 1.08] is therefore a selected-winner estimate reported on its selection data. Minor arithmetic note in the same table: 54.24 - 54.62 = -0.38 while -0.39 is printed, and 49.19 - 54.62 = -5.43 while -5.44 is printed, consistent with rounding of unreported underlying values but not reproducible from the printed ones.
issues.why_it_matters: The abstract's quality claim rests on this interval. Selection on the reporting data biases the point estimate optimistically and narrows the apparent risk, and with n = 60 the interval is already about +/-1.5 F1 wide. The paper is careful to disclaim equivalence, which mitigates but does not remove the issue.
issues.required_action: Either designate the headline policy on the calibration set before looking at validation, or report the selection procedure and state that the interval is not selection-corrected; add a sentence noting the multiplicity across six comparisons. Print unrounded F1 means so the delta column reproduces.
issues.verification_test: Re-report the frozen policy's delta and interval on a held-out cohort (e.g. Qasper/2WikiMQA indices outside 4-35) that played no role in policy selection, and check the interval is comparable.
issues.evidence_required: A held-out evaluation of the selected policy, or an explicit pre-registration of the selection rule.
issues.meta_reason: Adjudicated as actionable and folded into A2.

issues.location: Section 2 (p.3) 'CoMem persists one depth-j residual... (Liu et al., 2026a;b). We build on that interface'; references (p.10); Appendix A (p.12) 'QS Job 234340 / Trial 1830116'; Appendix A (p.13) 'Apple Mac16,8 CPU host'

The reference author list includes what appear to be handles rather than names ('Key', 'Rayying'). Appendix A discloses an internal job identifier ('QS Job 234340 / Trial 1830116') and a specific host machine model. Table 27 elsewhere shows anonymization awareness ('the anonymous package assigns a neutral artifact alias').
issues.why_it_matters: Third-person citation of prior work is normal and I make no accusation, but the combination of a foundational self-referential-reading citation, non-standard author entries, and internal job identifiers puts avoidable strain on double-blind review and on citation hygiene. It is fixable at zero cost to the science.
issues.required_action: Keep the CoMem citation but neutralize the framing (e.g. 'Q-CoMem adopts the CoMem split-replay interface'), correct the reference author entries to real names or drop the handles, and replace internal job/trial identifiers and host model strings in Appendix A with neutral aliases as already done for the HYPIC artifact.

issues.meta_reason: Third-person citation of the prior work one builds on is standard ICLR practice and is not an anonymity defect; treating it as one would penalise correct credit assignment, which is one of this paper's genuine strengths. Only the mechanical parts of the issue are actionable and I confirmed them in the PDF: the internal platform identifiers in Appendix A ('QS Job 234340 / Trial 1830116'), the named host machine model, and the pseudonymous entries ('Key', 'Rayying') in the CoMem reference.

issues.location: Reproducibility Statement (p.9); Appendix A (pp.12-13); Appendix I Table 27 (pp.29-31); Sec. 5.5 (pp.7-8)
issues.diagnosis: The paper's entire reproducibility apparatus resolves to a package that is never made available. Appendix I Table 27 gives ~30 relative paths 'rooted at the accompanying research package' (evidence/round_04_rr2_package/replay/run_replay.sh, evidence/qcomem_mixed_validation_60item_20260812d/, evidence/experiment_registry.json entries, ...). Nowhere in 31 pages is there an anonymous repository URL, a supplementary-material reference, or a sentence stating that the package is submitted: grep over the full text finds zero occurrences of 'supplementary', 'available', 'anonymized', 'github', 'zenodo', or any http artifact link. Consequently every quantitative statement in Sec. 5.5 and Appendix A is supported only by an assertion of having run something: 209,920 attention and 635,520 GDN call receipts; 96 configurations and 192 rebuilt cells; 288 fan-out comparisons; 144 / 12,960 / 3,840 / 24 selected-cell units; 96,660 relations and 1,080 receiver rows; 536 raw artifacts; a 1,367-node terminal tree; 44 clean rows and 44 rejected controls; 224 and 184 rejected negative controls; 272 sidecars totalling 140,199,936 bytes. I hold pdf_plus_repository access and was given only claim_evidence_map.tsv and method_provenance.tsv - two index files authored by the same pipeline - so I could not verify a single one of these counts against an artifact.
issues.why_it_matters: Roughly 40% of the main-text results section and most of the 22-page appendix consist of counts that no third party can re-derive, check, or falsify. Under the ICLR reviewer guide's reproducibility criterion this is the difference between evidence and testimony. It also makes the paper's central methodological selling point - that ForkAudit provides storage evidence rather than output equality - itself unauditable, which is precisely the failure mode the method is designed to prevent.
issues.required_action: Attach an anonymized artifact (or state the exact availability mechanism and timing) that at minimum contains: the primary replay package and its one-command run_replay.sh; the 60-item validation package with raw shards and the F1/bootstrap/Store recomputation; and the eight-item timing shards. Add a one-paragraph 'Artifact availability' block immediately after the Reproducibility Statement naming what is included, its size, its runtime, and what is intentionally excluded.
issues.verification_test: A reviewer downloads the artifact on a CPU-only host, runs the advertised one-command replay, and confirms that it terminates in the Appendix-A-reported ~100 s and reproduces at least: Table 1's six Store values and six F1 values, the four bootstrap intervals cited in the text, Table 2's six Store values, and the 54.5% allocator delta - each byte-identical to the manuscript.
issues.evidence_required: An anonymized artifact archive or repository link, plus a manifest mapping each numbered claim in the paper to a file inside it.
issues.meta_reason: The underlying finding is confirmed and material -- I verified the PDF contains no availability statement of any kind, and the two supplied index files cannot corroborate the Section 5.5 counts -- but the rhetorical scaling is not supported: the paper does bind its counts to internal hashes and manifests, and the counts are arithmetically self-consistent everywhere three reviewers checked. The actionable requirement is an artifact-availability paragraph and a resolvable index, not a wholesale discount of Section 5.5.

issues.location: Sec. 4.1-4.3 (pp.4-5), Eq. 2 and Eq. 3; Sec. 5.1-5.2 (pp.5-6); method_provenance.tsv (all 83 rows)

There is no entry for the groupwise quantizer of Eq. 3, the group size of 64, the BF16 scale/bias metadata layout, the offline Write that packs the complete entry at split depth j, the online Read that dequantizes and forks, the frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 state-type assignment, the per-layer bit search on the four-item calibration set, the LongBench F1 implementation, the paired 10,000-resample bootstrap, or the component-sum Store accounting used for Table 1. The two hits for 'Q4'/'Q8' are in M-MAC-CONTROL-DERIVATION, an unpooled Apple-M4 motivation table. The only row touching the deployment numbers, M-H20-DEPLOYMENT-DERIVATION, points at scripts/generate_h20_deployment_table.py with symbols 'main; sha256; require; format_mib' - a formatter that reads an already-frozen summary. Every other row maps to ForkAudit ownership code (qcomem_vllm_paged_kernel.py, qcomem_qwen35_native_cache.py, replay_rr2.py, ...), related-work transfer ports, or table generators. The asymmetry is total: the complementary audit component has exhaustive provenance and the named contribution has none.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's headline results - 14.10x smaller retained state at -0.39 F1 - are produced by code that the provenance artifact does not reference at all. A reader cannot confirm that Eq. 3 is what was executed, that the reported bit assignment matches the implementation, that Store was summed over the components Eq. 2 lists, or that F1 and the bootstrap follow the stated definitions. Method statements in Sec. 4.1-4.3 are therefore asserted, not backed. This inverts the paper's own thesis: it argues that output equality is insufficient because implementations can diverge silently from their described semantics, yet the described semantics of Q-CoMem itself are unbacked by any code reference.
issues.required_action: Add method_provenance rows (source path, symbol, configuration) for at minimum: the quantize/dequantize kernel implementing Eq. 3; the Write path that enumerates and packs the Eq. 2 components; the Read path (dequantize, fork, lower-layer replay, merge at j, suffix); the policy definitions for frozen Q4/Q4/Q8, same-memory per-layer, and aggressive mixed; the Store accounting function used for Table 1; and the F1 and bootstrap routines. Ship the corresponding files in the artifact.
issues.verification_test: Open the named quantizer source and confirm that group size is 64, that scale = (u - m) / (2^b - 1) with clipped rounding to [0, 2^b - 1], and that scale/bias are stored in BF16; then run the named Store accounting function over one archived document entry and confirm it returns 9.660873 MiB for the frozen policy and 136.235352 MiB for full-prefix Q16.
issues.evidence_required: Source files and symbol names for the Q-CoMem Write/Read/quantizer/policy/accounting/metric code, plus the config that pins split depth j = 7 and the bit vectors.

issues.location: Eq. 1 and Sec 3 p.3; Sec 5.1 'Memory denominators' p.6; Sec 5.6 p.8-9
claim_ids: retained document state is the controllable term
issues.diagnosis: Eq. 1 motivates the work by the size of the hot document set H that fits in a device budget. Every denominator in the paper explicitly excludes 'admitted serving capacity', 'process/NVML memory', and 'active workspace' (Sec 5.1, Table 2 footnote, Sec 5.6). Sec 5.6 states 'reducing Store does not by itself prove lower peak VRAM or serving capacity' and 'H20 is not an edge device'. No experiment varies |H| or reports how many documents remain resident at a fixed budget under any policy.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's own framing makes retained bytes valuable only through their translation into more resident documents, and that translation is placed outside every measurement. The contribution is therefore a proxy improvement whose practical payoff is argued from Eq. 1 rather than demonstrated, on hardware the authors themselves say is not the motivating deployment. Combined with Q1, this leaves the significance case resting on an un-baselined ratio measured in a quantity the paper says does not imply the outcome it motivates. The disclosure is honest, which is why this is major rather than critical, but honesty about a missing link does not supply the link.
issues.required_action: Add one experiment holding a device memory budget fixed and reporting the number of documents that stay resident, plus measured peak allocated memory, under full-prefix BF16, full-prefix Q4 (see Q1), and Q-CoMem Q4/Q4/Q8. Alternatively, soften Sec 3 and the Conclusion so that Eq. 1 is presented as motivation for the metric rather than as an outcome the paper advances.
issues.verification_test: A table with a fixed device budget on one axis and resident-document count plus peak allocated memory per policy on the other, or Sec 3 and the Conclusion rewritten to claim only the retained-byte metric.
issues.evidence_required: One residency-versus-budget sweep on the existing stack, or a claim softening.
issues.meta_reason: Adjudicated as actionable and folded into A13.

issues.location: Sec 2 'Hybrid state and cache management' p.3 (lines 125-131); Sec 4.2 Eq. 3 p.4; contribution bullet 1 p.2 (lines 084-087); Table 11 p.20
claim_ids: Complete quantized hybrid split state (contribution bullet 1)
Real groupwise Q4/Q8 packing and a state-type/per-layer bit assignment
issues.diagnosis: The Related Work paragraph covering cache compression cites exactly three works: Palu (low-rank projection), SqueezeAttention (layer-wise budget), and HeadKV (head-level budget). The full reference list contains no KV-cache quantization work of any kind. Yet the paper's own mechanism is quantization: Eq. 3 is standard asymmetric min-max affine quantization over 64-value groups with BF16 scale and bias, and Sec 4.2 assigns different bit widths per state type and per layer (vector [8,8,4,4,8,8,8]). Public literature I checked establishes group-wise 4-bit KV quantization (FlexGen), per-channel key / per-token value quantization (KIVI, KVQuant), grouped mixed-precision with outlier handling (Atom), and sensitivity-driven layer-wise mixed-precision KV quantization (KVTuner, ICML 2025). There is also published work on quantizing Mamba/SSM recurrent state caches reporting that quantization error accumulates through the recurrence and that recurrent state needs higher precision - which is exactly the Q8-for-GDN, Q4-for-attention asymmetry the paper adopts and presents without precedent.
issues.why_it_matters: This is the paper's core mechanism and a reader cannot judge what is new without the adjacent literature. Contribution bullet 1 foregrounds 'real groupwise Q4/Q8 packing and a state-type/per-layer bit assignment', both of which are established techniques; the defensible delta is only their application to the depth-j residual plus lower hybrid state under one honest accounting. Presenting the per-layer bit vector and the recurrent-state precision asymmetry as this paper's design surface, with no acknowledgment of the layer-wise mixed-precision KV quantization and SSM-cache quantization lines, overstates novelty by omission rather than by assertion. It also explains why Q1's baseline was never considered: the paper does not engage with the literature in which quantizing an exact cache is the standard move.
issues.required_action: Add a KV/state-quantization paragraph to Sec 2 covering group-wise, per-channel/per-token, and layer-wise mixed-precision KV quantization plus recurrent/SSM-state quantization, with citations. Rewrite contribution bullet 1 to claim only the application and accounting delta, not the quantizer or the idea of per-layer bit assignment. Add a row to Table 11 for the KV-quantization family stating the relation. State explicitly whether CoMem already quantized the residual.
issues.verification_test: The revised Sec 2 must name at least the group-wise, per-channel/per-token, and layer-wise mixed-precision KV quantization families and, for each, say in one sentence what Q-CoMem does differently. Contribution bullet 1 must no longer claim the packing scheme itself as a contribution.
issues.evidence_required: Literature only; no new experiments.
issues.meta_reason: Adjudicated as actionable and folded into A9.

issues.location: Table 2 p.6 versus Table 18 p.24; Table 5 p.16 ('CoMem Q8/Q4/mixed variants'); Table 13 p.21 ('CoMem BF16/Q8/Q4 split')
claim_ids: we build on that interface rather than claiming a new split-replay primitive
Q-CoMem is a capacity-first extension of CoMem split replay
issues.diagnosis: Table 2 and Table 18 report identical measurements (140.34 / 0.163 / 54.11 / 13.38 / 39.14; 15.89 / 0.673 / 55.44 / 7.15 / 39.14; 10.01 / 0.674 / 54.97 / 7.19 / 39.01; 9.74 / 0.673 / 55.07 / 7.19 / 39.11; 8.41 / 0.674 / 55.02 / 7.19 / 36.09) but Table 2 labels the rows 'Q-CoMem' while Table 18 labels the same rows 'CoMem state' and 'CoMem mixed state'. Using 'CoMem' as the row label for configurations measured in this paper erases that boundary in exactly the tables a reader consults to see the delta. Table 13 is the sharpest case: a reader cannot tell whether quantized CoMem variants at Q8 and Q4 predate this submission, and if they do, contribution bullet 1 shrinks to the lower-hybrid-state accounting alone.
