issues.location: Sec 5.1 'Latency execution' (p.6); Table 2 and its footnote (p.7); Sec 5.3 (p.6-7); Abstract (p.1, lines 027-030)
issues.diagnosis: The entire latency characterization rests on 8 items with 3 timing repeats each (24 measurements per configuration), and Table 2 reports only medians for Store, TTFT, TPOT and tok/s with no interquartile range, no min/max, no standard deviation, and no per-item values anywhere in the paper. I searched the full text for 'std', 'IQR', 'interquartile' and 'variance' and found none in connection with Table 2. No warmup procedure is described for this block (the only warmup mentioned in the paper is for the separate 24-cell HYPIC cohort, Appendix H p.28). The three timing metrics are also never defined: tok/s is not 1/TPOT (13.38 versus 18.48 for full-prefix; 7.19 versus 18.19 for Q-CoMem), and reconciling the three columns requires assuming a generated length of about 8 tokens that the paper never reports, even though the cap is 32. On this basis the paper makes a quantitative claim in its abstract ('TPOT is within 2.5% of its 54.11 ms value'), which rests on a 0.86-1.33 ms difference on a 54 ms quantity.
issues.why_it_matters: An 8-item, 3-repeat, median-only panel with no dispersion cannot support a quantitative statement about a 2.5% effect, and the reader has no way to judge whether 55.44 versus 54.11 ms is a real regression or measurement noise. The direction matters: 'within 2.5%' is the one favorable framing in an otherwise adverse latency story, and it is exactly the claim least supported by the reported statistics. The undefined tok/s column compounds this, because the reader cannot reconstruct end-to-end per-query cost from TTFT, TPOT and throughput, which is the quantity a deployment would care about.
issues.required_action: Report per-item and per-repeat values (or at minimum median with full range or IQR) for TTFT, TPOT and tok/s for every row of Table 2; state the warmup procedure and whether repeats are within-process; give the defining formula for each timing metric and the mean and range of generated tokens per item; and either drop the 'within 2.5%' phrasing or accompany it with the observed spread. Extend the timing execution to all 60 items so the latency panel is not an 8-item subset (see R44-4-06, which the same run would also fix).
issues.verification_test: Recompute each Table 2 cell from the 168 archived timing rows named in the artifact (M-H20-DEPLOYMENT-DERIVATION: '6 displayed in-process configurations with 24 timing measurements each'), and require that the paper reports the dispersion of each column. Independently check that median tok/s equals the stated formula applied to the archived per-item generated-token counts; if the reconstruction fails, the metric definitions are still wrong.
issues.evidence_required: Re-derivation from archived timing shards for dispersion and definitions; one extended run for the 60-item timing panel.
issues.meta_reason: Adjudicated as actionable and folded into A7.

issues.location: Sec 5.1 'Quality cohort' (p.5); Sec 5.6 (p.8); Appendix A (p.12); Appendix H (p.28); artifact method_provenance.tsv and claim_evidence_map.tsv
issues.diagnosis: The paper's single most decision-relevant table is also the least specified and least provenanced. The Sec 5.1 quality-cohort paragraph never states the split depth (j=7 appears only in Figure 2's caption and, for a different cohort, in Appendix Table 13), never states the decoding strategy (greedy is specified only for the 8-item execution), and never states the number of runs or repeats. The bootstrap is described only as '10,000-resample' with no method (percentile / basic / BCa), no resampling unit, and no seed; the artifact mentions '24 seeded paired-bootstrap intervals' but the seed is not in the PDF. Sec 5.6 and Appendix H concede that 'the original launcher used a mutable code directory and retained neither a pre-run full-source ledger nor a full model-weight ledger'. In the artifact, method_provenance.tsv contains no row at all for this panel: there is no method entry for the quantizer used, the LongBench F1 scorer, the bootstrap implementation, or the Table 1 Store component accounting, although comparable rows exist for the 8-item panel (M-H20-DEPLOYMENT-DERIVATION), the Mac control (M-MAC-CONTROL-DERIVATION) and the serving panel (M-RW-SERVING-DERIVATION). The claim_evidence_map's manuscript_locations field for all three C-QCOMEM-60-* claims reads 'Integrated in R42 and independently claim-audited on 2026-09-02' instead of naming a section or table.
issues.why_it_matters: A PDF-only reader cannot reconstruct the experiment that produces the paper's headline numbers: they do not know the depth, the decoder, the number of runs, or the interval construction. A repository reader cannot locate the code either, because the provenance file skips this panel entirely. The contrast with the rest of the paper is stark: ForkAudit results carry byte-level ledgers and hash-bound replay, while the capacity and quality result that the title and abstract rest on comes from an archival run whose source state is admittedly unverified. The authors deserve credit for disclosing this, but disclosure does not repair the gap, and it is easy to repair because the frozen-source 8-item pipeline already exists on the same stack.
issues.required_action: State the split depth, decoding strategy, number of runs per configuration, bootstrap method, resampling unit and seed in Sec 5.1. Re-run the 60-item panel under the frozen source and model ledger already used for the 8-item execution, which would simultaneously deliver TTFT on all 60 items (R44-4-03), a matched generation protocol (R44-4-07), and a single denominator (R44-4-09). Add method_provenance rows for the packer, scorer, bootstrap and Store accounting, and replace the placeholder manuscript_locations for the three C-QCOMEM-60-* claims with real section and table references.
issues.verification_test: Check that Sec 5.1 names j, the decoder, the repeat count, and the bootstrap method and seed. Re-run the archived verifier and require the 360 item-level F1 values and 24 intervals to reproduce bit-for-bit under the stated seed. In the artifact, require at least one method_provenance row whose manuscript_locations names Table 1, and require the C-QCOMEM-60-* rows to name a section and table rather than a process note.
issues.evidence_required: One source-frozen re-execution of the 60-item panel plus artifact metadata repair. Note: the provenance half of this issue is visible only in the repository, not in the PDF.

issues.location: Table 1 F1 column (p.6) versus Table 2 F1 column (p.7); Sec 5.1 (p.5-6); Table 18 (p.24)
issues.diagnosis: Full-prefix Q16/BF16 records F1 54.68 in Table 1 and F1 39.14 in Table 2, a gap of 15.5 points for the same model and the same configuration on 8 items drawn from the same 60. Both columns are labelled 'F1 (0-100)'. The gap is never mentioned in the paper. The most likely cause is visible but unsurfaced: Sec 5.1 says the quality cohort allows Qasper 'at most 128 generated tokens and 2WikiMQA at most 32', whereas the latency execution uses 'at most 32 generated tokens' for every item, so Qasper answers are truncated to a quarter of their allowed length in Table 2. The paper's non-pooling justification, repeated four times, is framed as a cohort and aggregation difference ('the execution and aggregation protocol is separate'), not as a generation-protocol difference that changes the metric's level.
issues.why_it_matters: A reader who compares the paper's two result tables on their two shared column names cannot do so on either one: 'Store' means different things (R44-4-09) and 'F1 (0-100)' is measured under different generation caps. Because the paper leans on the 8-item panel for the quality statements in Sec 5.4 ('Q8 records the same measured mean F1 of 39.137 as its full-prefix reference'), the reader needs to know that this panel operates in a truncated-answer regime where F1 is depressed by 15 points and where differences between policies may compress or expand relative to the 60-item regime. The 'not pooled' disclaimer is necessary but not sufficient: it explains that the numbers must not be averaged, not why they differ by 40% in level.
issues.required_action: State in Sec 5.1 and in Table 2's caption that the two panels use different generation caps for Qasper (128 vs 32) and that this, not sampling, explains the F1 level difference. Either re-run the 8 items under the 60-item caps so the two panels share a generation protocol, or add a matched-cap row so the reader can see the size of the protocol effect.
issues.verification_test: Re-score the 8-item predictions under the 60-item generation caps and confirm the full-prefix F1 moves from 39.14 toward the 60-item level; report the residual difference attributable to item selection. Require an explicit sentence naming the cap difference in Sec 5.1 or the Table 2 caption.
issues.evidence_required: One re-run or re-score of 8 items under the 60-item caps.

issues.location: Sec 5.1 'Memory denominators' (p.6); Table 1 footnote (p.6); Table 2 footnote (p.7); Sec G.1 text and Table 18 (p.24); Table 15 (p.21)
issues.diagnosis: The paper defines three incompatible accountings all reported under names built on 'Store' or memory: component sums of persistent parts (Table 1), the physical byte-range union owned by one retained entry (Table 2), and a post-priming allocator delta (Table 15). Sec 5.1 states they are not pooled. Two problems remain. First, the size of the gap between the first two is never quantified even though matched configurations exist: full-prefix reads 136.235 (component) versus 140.34 (byte-range), and the Q4/Q4/Q8 policy reads 9.661 versus 10.01, about 3% apart; stating this would strengthen the paper and is currently left for the reader to derive. Second, Sec G.1 does compute a cross-cohort ratio: 'Prefix Cache and HYPIC retain 8.78x and 20.39x as much Store as CoMem Q8, respectively, under the separate Store estimand' (139.53/15.89 = 8.78, 324.09/15.89 = 20.40). Those HYPIC/Prefix numbers come from a receipt-instrumented SGLang 0.5.14 radix-cache lifecycle (Table 5 'HYPIC retained-state receipts' row; artifact M-R34-HYPIC-STORE-RECEIPT) while 15.89 comes from the in-process Transformers execution, so this is a cross-runtime, cross-instrumentation, cross-cache-structure ratio in a paper whose stated rule is that these cohorts are unpooled and whose own Table 18 caption says only that 'timing is compared only within blocks'.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper asks the reader to accept a strict non-pooling discipline as the guarantor of its memory numbers, then performs the one cross-cohort arithmetic operation that discipline forbids, and does so at the point where the comparison is most flattering (a 20.39x advantage over HYPIC). Whether an entry-owned byte-range union is even commensurable between a paged radix allocator and a contiguous packed entry is not established anywhere. Meanwhile the one cross-denominator comparison that is both safe and informative, the ~3% gap between the two accountings on matched configurations, is omitted.
issues.required_action: Either drop the 8.78x/20.39x cross-runtime ratio and state the three Store values without dividing them, or add an explicit argument (and, ideally, a same-runtime control) that the byte-range-union estimand is measured identically under SGLang radix caching and under the in-process Transformers path. Separately, measure both accountings on the same retained entries and report the observed component-versus-byte-range gap in Sec 5.1, so the ~3% difference between 136.235/140.34 and 9.661/10.01 is documented rather than inferred.
issues.verification_test: Instrument one configuration with both accountings simultaneously and report the two numbers for the same entry; require the paper to state the measured gap. For the cross-runtime ratio, require either its removal or a documented equivalence test showing that the byte-range union of a radix-cached prefix and of a packed Q-CoMem entry are counted under identical inclusion rules.
issues.evidence_required: One dual-instrumented run on an existing configuration; no new cohort.
issues.meta_reason: Adjudicated as actionable and folded into A8.

issues.location: Sec. 5.1 'Memory denominators' (p.6); Table 1 footnote (p.6); Table 2 footnote (p.7); Sec. 5.2 (p.6); Sec. 5.6 (p.9)
issues.diagnosis: The paper's headline estimand is measured two different ways whose divergence is disclosed but never quantified. Sec. 5.1: 'the 60-item panel sums the stored persistent components (packed residual data, scales, biases, and unique lower-cache tensor storage), whereas the eight-item execution measures the physical byte-range union owned by one retained entry.' On the same model, stack, token cap, and split depth, full-prefix Q16 is 136.235 MiB/doc in Table 1 and 140.34 MiB/doc in Table 2 (a 3.0% gap), and the same frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 policy is 9.661 MiB/doc in Table 1 and 10.01 MiB/doc in Table 2 (a 3.6% gap). Crucially, Table 2's eight items are a declared strict subset of Table 1's sixty (indices 6-9 of each dataset, stated in Sec. 5.1 and in Table 2's title), so this is not a cohort-composition artifact that cannot be untangled - both accountings are computable on the same eight documents. The paper's response is only to refuse pooling; the two derived compression figures it then quotes side by side in Sec. 5.2 (14.10x from one denominator, 92.87%/93.06% from the other) are not on a common scale.
issues.why_it_matters: A capacity-first paper must have one auditable definition of retained bytes. Without a cross-walk, a reader cannot tell whether the 3% divergence is definitional (metadata, alignment, shared storage attributed differently) or empirical (different packing behaviour between the two executions), and cannot combine the tables even mentally. It also blocks any external comparison: the HYPIC 8.78x/20.39x ratios in Table 18 use the byte-range estimand, while the paper's headline 14.10x uses the component estimand.
issues.required_action: Compute both accountings on the eight shared items and add a short reconciliation table (component sum, byte-range union, and their difference decomposed into alignment/padding/shared-storage/metadata terms) for at least full-prefix Q16, split Q16, and frozen Q4/Q4/Q8. Then state which estimand is canonical for the paper's headline number.
issues.verification_test: Run both accounting implementations over the archived retained entries for source indices 6-9 of each dataset and confirm the reported per-item values and their difference; the reconciliation must account for the full 136.235 vs 140.34 and 9.661 vs 10.01 gaps within stated rounding.

issues.location: Sec. 5.1 'Quality cohort' and 'Latency execution' (pp.5-6); Table 1 (p.6); Table 2 (p.7); Sec. 5.3 (pp.6-7)

(a) The decoding rule for the 60-item cohort is never stated; 'greedy decoding' appears only in the latency paragraph, Table 2, and Tables 18-19, so Table 1's decoding is unspecified. (b) Table 2's footnote says 'Store and timing/throughput columns are medians' without naming the population: 8 items, 3 repeats, 24 measurements, or a median of per-item medians. (c) 'generated-token throughput' is never defined. The three timing columns are mutually consistent only under tok/s = n / (TTFT + n x TPOT); solving that relation gives n = 7.90 for full-prefix Q16, 7.97-8.02 for the four Q-CoMem rows, and 7.50 for dense - i.e. about eight generated tokens per item against a stated cap of 32. The actual generated lengths, which fully determine the throughput column, are never reported. (d) The 'aggressive mixed' row of Table 1 (7.536 MiB/doc, 18.08x, -5.44 F1, 5/60 catastrophic) has no stated bit assignment anywhere in the paper, so that row cannot be reproduced at all. issues.why_it_matters: These are exactly the parameters that decide whether a re-run lands on 54.24 or somewhere else. Item (c) matters most: throughput is the metric the abstract uses to characterise the cost of the method, and it is reported without a definition, without dispersion, and without the token counts that drive it. Item (d) makes a row that the paper uses to argue against aggressive quantization non-reproducible.

issues.location: Eq. 1 and Sec. 3 (p.3); Sec. 5.2 (p.6); Sec. 5.5 'Allocator reduction' (p.8); Sec. 5.6 (p.9)
issues.diagnosis: The paper motivates itself with Eq. 1, in which the controllable term is the sum of S(D) over the hot document set H, and argues that 'the retained term is the only one that grows with how many documents a deployment keeps warm'. No experiment ever varies |H|, measures how many documents fit, or measures peak device memory under the quantized policy. Sec. 5.6 states outright that 'reducing Store does not by itself prove lower peak VRAM or serving capacity', and the abstract disclaims lower total process memory. The single measurement that touches an allocator (Sec. 5.5: 4.901 -> 2.229 GiB at N = 32, 54.5%) comes from the ownership factorial, uses a third denominator, varies KV sharing rather than quantization (Table 15 shows 'Full-copy KV / Materialized GDN' vs 'Shared-doc KV / Materialized GDN'), and Sec. 5.6 states that the two reductions 'are not additive or interchangeable'. Sec. 5.6 further excludes continuous batching, QPS, admission, eviction, and scheduler effects. So the deployment budget the paper introduces to justify the work is never instantiated with the method the paper proposes.
issues.why_it_matters: Without a capacity measurement the contribution reduces to an improvement in a proxy that the paper itself declines to connect to any deployment consequence. The honest scoping is commendable but does not substitute for evidence; a reader cannot tell whether 14.10x smaller retained payload translates into more resident documents, because the Store estimand excludes allocator pools, active workspace, and process memory - the terms that typically dominate whether an extra document fits.
issues.required_action: Add one resident-document sweep on the reported stack: hold the model and a fixed request shape constant, admit documents 1, 2, 4, 8, ... until failure under full-prefix Q16, split Q16, and frozen Q4/Q4/Q8, and report the maximum resident document count and the peak allocator bytes as a function of |H|. This is the smallest experiment that connects Eq. 1 to the method and does not require new datasets or new baselines.
issues.verification_test: Report max resident documents per policy and a peak-memory-versus-|H| curve; confirm that the slope of retained bytes per document matches the Table 1 Store values and state the observed intercept (weights + workspace + runtime).
issues.evidence_required: A capacity sweep with peak allocator and, ideally, process/NVML memory alongside the Store proxy.
issues.meta_reason: Adjudicated as actionable and folded into A13.

issues.location: Table 1 (p.6) vs Table 2 (p.7); Section 5.1 'Memory denominators' (p.6, lines 294-301); Section 5.2 (p.6); Abstract (p.1)

issues.location: Eq. 1 and Section 3 (p.3); Section 5.1 'Memory denominators' (p.5); Section 5.6 (p.8); Section 6 (p.9) 'the one term of the deployment budget in Eq. 1 that scales with the hot document set'
issues.diagnosis: Eq. 1 is a device-byte inequality: M_device >= M_weights + M_shared + M_active + sum_D S(D) + M_runtime. But the measured S(D) in Tables 1 and 2 is a logical tensor payload that Section 5.1 says excludes non-tensor/Python metadata, allocator pools, process/NVML memory, active workspace and admission capacity, and Section 5.6 concedes that 'reducing Store does not by itself prove lower peak VRAM or serving capacity'. Meanwhile the paper demonstrates it can measure exactly the missing quantity - Appendix Table 15 reports final and peak allocated deltas above a frozen post-priming baseline - but applies that instrument only to the ownership factorial, never to a Q-CoMem quantized entry. Note also that Q4 packing produces many small tensors plus per-group BF16 scale and bias arrays, which is precisely the allocation pattern where caching-allocator overhead and fragmentation diverge most from logical payload; a 14.10x logical reduction could easily be a much smaller device-byte reduction.
issues.why_it_matters: The motivation, the method and the conclusion are all framed in terms of the Eq. 1 term, but no measurement of that term is ever reported for Q-CoMem. The gap is not disclosed as a mere caveat - it is the difference between 'we reduce the thing that limits how many documents fit' and 'we reduce a logical byte count that may or may not track the thing that limits how many documents fit'. Because the instrument already exists in the paper, this is a missing experiment rather than an infeasible one, which weakens the excuse for leaving it out.
issues.required_action: Report, for at least full-prefix Q16, split Q16 and frozen Q4/Q4/Q8, the allocated and peak device bytes for a fixed number of resident documents under the Table 15 denominator, and state the realized reduction of the Eq. 1 term next to the 14.10x logical figure. If the two diverge, report both and let the logical number be an upper bound. In the abstract, qualify 14.10x as retained tensor payload (which the paper already does) and add the measured device-byte reduction if it differs materially.
issues.verification_test: Prime the process, snapshot torch.cuda.memory_allocated and max_memory_allocated, admit K in {1, 4, 16} documents under each retention policy, snapshot again, and report deltas. Separately report documents-admitted-before-OOM at a fixed device budget for each policy. The claim 'quantization increases hot-document capacity' is verified only if documents-before-OOM scales with the logical reduction.
issues.evidence_required: Allocator and peak-memory deltas per retention policy at several residency counts, and ideally a documents-per-device capacity measurement.

issues.location: Figure 2a (p.4) 'lower prefix [0,7)', 'L7-L39 33-layer online suffix'; Section 4.3 (p.5); Section 5.3 (p.6); Section 5.6 (p.8)
issues.diagnosis: The split is fixed at j = 7 of L = 40, so Read skips 7/40 = 17.5% of the layers of a full prefill and must execute layers [7,40) over document plus query. The measured TTFT (0.673 s) is consistent with that structure: 0.825 x 0.649 s = 0.535 s of suffix work plus roughly 0.14 s of dequantization and overhead. j is never justified anywhere in the paper, no sweep over j is reported, and the structural ceiling on prefill savings is never stated. The one place a depth trade-off could be inspected, Appendix Table 13, is a different device and model and reports only a 1.15x online-time ratio at depth 7.
issues.why_it_matters: j is the single most important design parameter of a split-replay system: it sets both the retained-entry size and the online replay cost, and the paper's entire capacity-latency story is a function of it. Fixing it at 7 without justification or sensitivity analysis makes the reported operating point unfalsifiable as a design choice, and it hides from the reader that no amount of quantizer engineering can make Read cheaper than 82.5% of a dense prefill at this depth. Combined with T-01, this is why the reported point sits on the wrong side of the dense endpoint.
issues.required_action: State the structural bound explicitly in Section 4.1 or 4.3 (Read executes L - j of L layers, so prefill saving is at most j/L before dequantization cost). Add a sweep over j - at minimum j in {7, 13, 20, 27} - reporting retained Store, TTFT, and F1 for each, so the reader can see where, if anywhere, the trade-off becomes favourable against both endpoints. If deeper splits are infeasible because the retained entry grows, show that explicitly.
issues.verification_test: For each j, measure retained Store per document and TTFT on the same eight items, and plot Store against TTFT with the dense and full-prefix endpoints marked. Verify whether any j yields a point that is not dominated by the Section-3-conformant dense endpoint on (Store, end-to-end latency, F1).
issues.evidence_required: A depth sweep with Store, TTFT and F1 per j; and a statement of what constrains j in the Qwen3.5 hybrid geometry (e.g. attention/GDN layer placement).
issues.meta_reason: Adjudicated as actionable and folded into A14.

issues.location: Table 1 p.6 versus Table 2 p.6; Sec 5.4 p.7 (lines 351-353)

issues.location: Sec 2 'Hybrid state and cache management' p.3 (lines 125-131)
claim_ids: Q-CoMem differs by jointly accounting for the split residual and the lower hybrid state
issues.diagnosis: The hybrid thread in Sec 2 stops at Marconi (MLSys 2025) and HYPIC (arXiv 2607.01299). Public search surfaces contemporaneous arXiv work on the same design space that is neither cited nor discussed: position-independent caching for hybrid LLMs via a single cached initial state per linear layer (arXiv 2608.11231); prefix caching for hybrid LLMs that reconstructs linear-attention state by replaying only a short recent suffix of the prefix (arXiv 2608.30310); and decay-aware compression of hybrid recurrent-state checkpoints reporting 2.63x state compression with TTFT and throughput gains (arXiv 2608.30386). The last two are close to Q-CoMem's own moves - replaying a suffix to reconstruct hybrid state, and compressing retained hybrid recurrent state.
issues.why_it_matters: None of these is strictly prior art at an early-September submission, so this does not undercut novelty. But a reader assessing whether the split-replay-plus-compression design point is distinctive needs to know it is now crowded, and the closest of these works reports state compression with a TTFT improvement rather than a TTFT regression, which is directly relevant to how this paper's trade-off should be judged.
issues.required_action: Add a short concurrent-work paragraph to Sec 2 distinguishing Q-CoMem's depth-split plus whole-entry quantization from state-composition approaches and from decay-aware state compression, and noting which report TTFT gains rather than regressions.
issues.verification_test: Revised Sec 2 names the concurrent works and states in one sentence each how Q-CoMem's retained-state definition and its TTFT position differ.
issues.evidence_required: Literature only.
issues.meta_reason: Asserted from a reviewer-side search under pdf_only access and not verifiable from anything in the review record; REV-1 itself concedes none is prior art at this submission date. The related-work gap that IS verifiable and actionable is the absence of any KV/state-quantization citation whatsoever (Q2), which I confirmed against the reference list. Authors must not be required to cite specific unverifiable identifiers; a concurrent-work sentence is optional, the quantization-literature paragraph is not.
